name: Insanely Cool Tools

sources.title: Homepage — returns an empty JS shell to automated fetch; site is JavaScript-rendered
Submit route — resolves (200) but renders no content to non-JS fetches; submission form is client-side
Newsletter issue (search-indexed; Substack blocks direct fetch) — 'Get YOUR project featured! Click here to submit your project… in-front of 20,000+ startup founders, indie-makers and creators'
NavifyAI profile — submission is free, <1 minute, 3-5 tools featured per weekly email; contact jr@startups.fyi
LaunchPedia — free submission, featured plans available to skip queue; ~20k newsletter subs, 40% open rate, 10k+ monthly visitors (their figures)

conditions: Submission itself is free, but the payoff — being one of the 3-5 tools in the weekly newsletter — is editorially gated; paid 'featured plans' exist to skip the queue
requirements: Product must be a tool/app/website that fits a 'cool tools' curation for founders and indie makers
Account creation required per BacklinkBot's submission guide
Newsletter feature is selective — only 3-5 tools per weekly issue
preparation: Product name, URL, short description, logo
A one-line 'why it's insanely cool' angle — this is a curation, not a database dump
workflow: Open https://insanelycooltools.com/submit-tool in a JS-capable browser (the form does not render without JavaScript)
Create an account, enter product name, URL, description, logo
Submit for free; the listing joins the directory and the editorial queue for the weekly newsletter
Optionally take a featured plan to skip the queue
watchFor: Site is JS-rendered and the Substack newsletter subdomain blocks bots — verify the form in a real browser before assuming it works
Free listing ≠ newsletter feature; the 20k-subscriber email is the actual reach, and only a handful of tools make each issue
Featured/queue-skip upsells exist — confirm what the free tier actually includes before paying
Operated by the same person as startups.fyi (jr@startups.fyi listed as contact)
countsAsLive: The tool has a public listing page on insanelycooltools.com, and the stronger proof is appearing as a featured tool in a weekly Insanely Cool Tools newsletter issue
unknowns: Exact form fields (form is JS-rendered and could not be inspected)
Review turnaround and acceptance rate for free submissions
Whether directory links are dofollow (third-party lists claim yes, unverified)
